subject.title: Feature Request: Batch API support for background tasks

question: Should OpenClaw introduce a shared delayed-turn provider contract, with isolated cron agentTurn as the initial supported caller, or keep provider batch execution outside the core runtime for now?
rationale: The request requires new public provider/runtime and configuration surfaces plus explicit choices about delivery, cancellation, fallback, authentication, and which background callers are supported.

options.title: Adopt a bounded delayed-turn seam
options.body: Define an additive provider and Plugin SDK lifecycle, initially expose it only to isolated cron agentTurn jobs, and add provider implementations after the contract is approved.

options.title: Defer core support
options.body: Keep batch submission external until maintainers want to own a durable delayed agent-turn lifecycle and its compatibility contract.

options.title: Pursue a plugin-only prototype
options.body: Allow a narrowly scoped external experiment only if it can use existing public seams without creating parallel core execution semantics.

recommendation.title: Adopt a bounded delayed-turn seam
recommendation.body: Define an additive provider and Plugin SDK lifecycle, initially expose it only to isolated cron agentTurn jobs, and add provider implementations after the contract is approved.

likelyOwner.reason: Current provider/runtime and cron history plus the recent substantive issue review make this the strongest available routing candidate.
